messages:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed the console quota dashboard is double-counting requests for routes when clients use the TS SDK v2 routeMeta field.
Ashley: whoa, double-counting how? snapshot or per-token?
Maya: Per-request. Requests are attributed to both the canonical route and a fallback route in the console. Quota burn looks 2x for some customers.
Derek: That sounds like the route negotiation shim is emitting both a `route-hint` header and a `route-meta` body entry, and our console reconciler is treating them as separate route keys.
Maya: Exactly. Example from logs: `X-Route-Hint: tenant/alpha#canary` and body: `route_meta: { "route": "tenant/alpha" , "policy": "canary" }`. Console's mapping layer normalizes differently.
Ashley: Any chance this is telemetry sampling mismatch? if the console dedup relies on sampled ids we could miss join keys.
Derek: I dug in — the dedup uses `route_key_v2` when header present, `route_key_v1` when only body present. If both present it indexes both and increments two buckets.
Samir: Oof. Customers saw 30% higher burn on a canary they were testing. Ops pinged us.
Maya: Quick repro: curl to staging with both header+body.
Maya: ```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'X-Route-Hint: tenant/alpha#canary' \
  -d '{"input":"hi","route_meta":{"route":"tenant/alpha","policy":"canary"}}' \
  https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Ashley: Proposed fixes: 1) console normalization: prefer header over body and dedupe 2) small SDK change: stop sending header when route_meta present 3) telemetry patch: emit canonical route id so console can join reliably.
Derek: We need a short-term rollback path. Can we change console to dedupe in-place (hotfix) while SDK change ships next week?
Samir: For customers on Dedicated, headers are coming from proxies. That means console-hotfix only helps hosted routes; dedicated will still double-count unless proxy shim changes.
Ashley: Then prioritize console hotfix + a small feature flag `redwood.console.dedupe.route_keys` we enable for hosted only.
Maya: I'll open a console PR to prefer header and ignore body when both exist. Low risk.
Derek: I'll file an SDK issue. We should add an opt-in telemetry header `X-Route-Canonical` that always carries a canonical id (string) so console join is straightforward.
Samir: Agree on `X-Route-Canonical`. We can backfill proxies to set it for Dedicated.
Ashley: UX note — the console should also show a small yellow badge when route attribution is ambiguous (i) so SRE/customer knows to expect variance.
Maya: Good call. I can add UI hint and a small tooltip pointing to docs.
Derek: Rolling plan: console hotfix (canary in staging today, rollout tomorrow), SDK patch (minor semver, release next Tue), proxy shim for Dedicated (ops track).
Samir: Ops: I'll coordinate proxy rollout, need a 2-hour maintenance window.
Ashley: Telemetry: add an event `route_attribution_mismatch` to capture if we see multiple keys for same request id. Low overhead.
sre-bot: deploybot: canary started for console-hotfix on staging at 1719001500, tests passing. :rocket:
Maya: Thanks — let's reconvene after staging canary (say 1719001899) and confirm metrics.
Derek: I'll leave a unit test to assert dedupe behavior and add an integration check to the telemetry pipeline.
Maya: Filing threads: console PR #4921, sdk issue #2413, proxy ticket OPS-789.
Ashley: Thanks team — good catch. Small UX/telemetry changes will save customers from surprise burn. :thumbsup:
